channel.title: DevPulse · Security
channel.description: Daily security stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: Cloudflare Containers exposed residual disk blocks across tenants
item.description: Researchers showed that a customer could recover residual disk blocks previously used by Containers on the same host, though they could not target a specific customer or workload. The fleet-wide fix and constrained exposure make this a useful case in multi-tenant isolation.

item.title: File-notification monitoring enables keystroke timing and password-prompt spoofing
item.description: Researchers demonstrate that file-notification monitoring can reveal inter-keystroke timing and help spoof KDE authentication prompts; a kernel fix partially mitigates the issue. The techniques show how metadata access can expose user activity even without permission to read files.

item.title: XSS in SourceHut build logs enabled account takeover
item.description: A flaw in ansi2html allowed cross-site scripting through SourceHut build logs and led to account takeover. Engineers running CI or log-rendering services should consider how terminal formatting can turn untrusted build output into executable content.

item.title: Avast driver exploit turns a double-fetch flaw into SYSTEM access on Windows 11
item.description: The exploit chain turns a double-fetch bug in Avast’s kernel driver into an arbitrary kernel read/write primitive, then escalates to SYSTEM through token theft. Its heap-spray and cleanup details offer useful lessons for kernel exploit mitigations, though it concerns one product.

item.title: Self-decrypting HTML packages air-gapped file encryption with OpenPGP signatures
item.description: The single-file tool decrypts offline in a browser, embeds OpenPGP signatures and aims for reproducible builds, though the author notes an OS dependency. Its design offers a useful case for engineers balancing portability, auditability and secure file sharing.
